fraud.title: Finding fraud in the noise
fraud.lede: A rare-event model that makes the tradeoff between missed fraud and review workload visible.
fraud.question: Which suspicious transactions deserve an analyst’s attention?
fraud.purpose: Choose an investigation policy with its review workload and missed cases in view.
fraud.role: Rare-event modelling · evaluation design · decision interface
fraud.data: Worldline / ULB anonymized transactions: 284,807 source rows, 283,726 after deduplication. The later test partition contains 56,746 transactions and 74 fraud labels.
fraud.approach: Chronological partitions keep later transactions out of development. The model is fitted on 45%, calibrated on an independent 15%, selected on 20%, then evaluated on the final 20%.

decisions.title: Evaluate later transactions
decisions.body: Chronological partitions preserve the direction of time. Later test transactions stay outside fitting, calibration and threshold selection.

decisions.title: Keep probability calibration independent
decisions.body: A separate reserve calibrates the fitted model. Validation selects the primary F2 threshold and review-budget policies before their test outcomes are inspected.

decisions.title: Show the operating trade-off
decisions.body: Average precision describes ranking. The gallery and lab also reveal the actual number of captured fraud cases, false flags and missed cases at each frozen policy.

findings: The primary F2 policy finds 55 of 74 fraud cases and makes six false flags; 19 fraud cases remain missed.
A separate 0.2% validation-budget policy finds 59 test fraud cases with 53 false flags. Its workload differs from the primary policy.
Estimated recall has uncertainty. Relative error costs are assumptions; these results do not measure money recovered.
fraud.next: An independent, later-period sample and real investigation costs would be needed before choosing a business operating policy.
limitations: A two-day historical benchmark, with anonymized features and only 74 fraud cases in the test set.
An independent, later-period sample and real investigation costs would be needed before choosing a business operating policy.

additionalImages.caption: Precision and recall describe the selected model on the later test partition. Its primary frozen threshold is separate from the review-budget policies.
Policies are chosen on validation. The chart reports their test workload and fraud capture; ties can leave a budget partly unused or change its realized test workload.
Score distributions use the test cohort. Fraud is rare, and its anonymized features prevent a direct business explanation of an individual transaction.

fraud.rights: ODbL / DbCL dataset rights; attribution retained.

churn.title: Understanding the signals around departure
churn.lede: An employee-departure classifier with stable feature associations, error analysis, and a clear boundary around future use.
churn.question: What does a departure benchmark reveal, and what does it leave unanswered?
churn.purpose: Examine model behavior and audit whether the required features would be available before departure.
churn.role: Classification workflow · calibration · error and feature audits
churn.data: The public HR benchmark contains 14,999 source rows and 11,991 unique records. The held-out test partition contains 2,399 rows and 398 departure labels.
churn.approach: Deduplication precedes splitting. Fitting, calibration, validation and test remain separate. Development-only permutation importance checks feature-rank stability.

decisions.title: Remove repeated records before splitting
decisions.body: The source contains duplicate rows. Deduplicating before partitioning prevents identical employee records from entering both development and evaluation.

decisions.title: Audit the score as well as the label
decisions.body: Independent calibration, review policies, error slices and development-only importance checks give the benchmark an evidence trail beyond a single accuracy figure.

decisions.title: Keep associations in context
decisions.body: Feature rankings describe this benchmark. The absence of observation dates and an explicit departure horizon prevents a claim that these inputs predict future employee behavior.

findings: At its frozen threshold, the model identifies 360 of 398 departure labels with eight false flags; 38 departures remain missed.
Satisfaction, tenure, project count and monthly hours have strong development-set associations. Those associations do not establish causes.
Calibration and subgroup errors help inspect behavior; a random benchmark holdout cannot prove future-company performance.
churn.next: Use dated employee snapshots, a defined departure horizon, and an independent company cohort before testing any workplace application.
limitations: The benchmark has no employee IDs, observation dates, or validated prediction horizon.
Use dated employee snapshots, a defined departure horizon, and an independent company cohort before testing any workplace application.

additionalImages.caption: Importance ranks come from development-only checks. A feature association does not establish that changing it will prevent a departure.
Departure recall and false-flag behavior are measured by department in the held-out test set. Wilson intervals do not cover company shift or undocumented feature timing.
Calibration compares score bands with observed test departure rates. These are retrospective benchmark observations, not a validated future prediction horizon.

sourceLinks.label: Results report at the reviewed revision

churn.rights: CC0 as declared by the dataset publisher; source provenance remains limited.

sentiment.title: Listening beyond a positive or negative label
sentiment.lede: Three-class sentiment analysis with human labels, a transparent baseline, and visible error patterns.
sentiment.question: How reliably can short social posts be classified by sentiment?
sentiment.purpose: Understand which classifications merit human review before aggregating customer feedback.
sentiment.role: Text modelling · benchmark design · interpretable error analysis
sentiment.data: TweetEval / SemEval-2017 sentiment: 59,899 source posts. After development overlap cleanup, all 12,284 official test posts remain intact.
sentiment.approach: Text preprocessing and vocabulary are fitted on development data. Validation macro F1 selects the three-class TF-IDF model before the official test set is evaluated.

decisions.title: Use the task’s human labels
decisions.body: The current three-class benchmark evaluates negative, neutral and positive sentiment against TweetEval’s official human labels, rather than treating automated labels as ground truth.

decisions.title: Select before inspecting test performance
decisions.body: Validation macro F1 selects the TF-IDF model. Another candidate’s test score does not retroactively change the chosen model.

decisions.title: Expose the difficult class boundary
decisions.body: The confusion matrix makes negative-to-neutral mistakes visible. Class support and recall help explain what the overall score hides; authored demo examples do not claim to be collected customer evidence.

findings: The selected model reaches 58.2% accuracy and 0.5587 macro F1. VADER reaches 53.0% accuracy and 0.5288 macro F1 on the same three-class test task.
Negative-to-neutral confusion is a major weakness: 2,008 of 3,972 negative posts are classified as neutral.
Mixed wording and sarcasm can challenge a lexical model. Heuristic diagnostic tags are not human annotations of sarcasm or mixed sentiment.
sentiment.next: A separately labelled, representative sample from the intended customer channel would be needed to validate a feedback workflow.

metrics.label: Macro F1
metrics.context: Equal emphasis on the three classes

limitations: Historical social posts; no measurement of Black Friday public opinion or current customer sentiment.
A separately labelled, representative sample from the intended customer channel would be needed to validate a feedback workflow.

sourceLinks.label: Results report at the reviewed revision

sentiment.rights: Upstream redistribution licence unspecified; raw social-post text stays local. Demo text is authored.

ctr.title: Putting attention where the signal is
ctr.lede: A ranking study that prioritizes useful enrichment over a misleading accuracy headline.
ctr.question: Can a model concentrate observed clicks in a smaller set of ad contexts?
ctr.purpose: Assess whether ranking can prioritize a smaller set of benchmark contexts for further investigation.
ctr.role: Grouped evaluation · ranking analytics · probability diagnostics
ctr.data: OpenML / Tencent KDD benchmark: 39,926 deduplicated contexts. The group-isolated test partition contains 7,984 rows and 1,391 click labels.
ctr.approach: Known users and anonymous contexts remain disjoint across fit, calibration, validation and test. Validation log loss selects the logistic model; ranking budgets are evaluated separately.

decisions.title: Isolate repeated user contexts
decisions.body: Known users and anonymous context groups cannot cross fit, calibration, validation and test. User IDs and aggregate impression counts are excluded from the input features.

decisions.title: Measure ranking and probability quality
decisions.body: Validation log loss selects the logistic model. The evaluation separately reports calibration, average precision and fixed-budget click-label enrichment.

decisions.title: Respect the sampling boundary
decisions.body: Negative downsampling changes the base rate. Enrichment is stated relative to this test set; neither the model scores nor ad-position edits establish population CTR or a causal advertising effect.

findings: The highest-scoring 799 test contexts contain 269 of 1,391 observed clicks: 19.3% capture in approximately 10% of rows.
That selection gives 1.93× enrichment relative to the test prevalence. Log loss is 0.4411 versus a 0.4627 prior baseline.
Sampled benchmark scores cannot establish population CTR, revenue lift, or the outcome of moving an ad to another position.
ctr.next: Representative impression logs, timestamps and an independent campaign evaluation would be needed before interpreting scores as real campaign probabilities.
limitations: The benchmark has downsampled negatives and no representative campaign timelines or population click rate.
Representative impression logs, timestamps and an independent campaign evaluation would be needed before interpreting scores as real campaign probabilities.

watch.title: A collection becomes a conversation.
watch.lede: An archival watch catalog, transformed into an explorable visual atlas.
watch.question: How can someone discover patterns across a catalog without losing the individual reference?
watch.purpose: Connect a high-level collection view to the watches that explain it.
watch.role: Data normalization · interactive catalog · visual storytelling
watch.data: Seven source tables describe 1,629 wristwatch references across five watchmakers. The catalog represents an archival 2023–2024 snapshot.
watch.approach: Normalize brands and references into one collection model, then connect search, filters and chart selections to the matching reference cards.

decisions.title: Use one reference model
decisions.body: The catalog and insights share normalized brand and reference fields, so the visual overview and the individual watches remain connected.

decisions.title: Turn charts into an entry point
decisions.body: Chart selections lead to relevant watch references. Case dimensions, movement families and collection mix become useful ways to explore the catalog.

decisions.title: Give the snapshot a clear boundary
decisions.body: The interface presents archival specifications and inferred segment labels without implying live inventory, current prices or market value.

findings: The reviewed catalog contains 1,629 references across five watchmakers.
Search, filters and linked insights connect collection patterns to individual references.
A public application lets visitors inspect the interaction directly, alongside the captured interface.
limitations: The underlying catalog is a 2023–2024 archival snapshot.
Segment labels are inferred. Specifications and prices are not live market data.
watch.next: Refresh source provenance and reconcile specification changes before presenting any live purchasing or valuation workflow.

playerpulse.title: A fairer way to compare the game.
playerpulse.lede: A comparison workspace that makes age, minutes and metric coverage part of the story.
playerpulse.question: How do footballers compare when age and playing time are held in view?
playerpulse.purpose: Make football comparisons more transparent by aligning the available age and metric coverage.
playerpulse.role: React interface · sports data pipelines · comparison design
playerpulse.evidenceType: Local project capture · recorded player archive
playerpulse.data: The portfolio explorer uses five players from the saved club-league archive, with recorded goals, assists and minutes. The full local project also contains World Cup views and a permission-gated match-log pipeline.
playerpulse.approach: Align player records by age, calculate per-90 rates from recorded minutes, and expose missing records instead of silently filling the gaps.

decisions.title: Align the comparison by age
decisions.body: Age gives visitors a consistent comparison frame. The visible records change together as the selected age changes.

decisions.title: Keep playing time visible
decisions.body: Per-90 rates complement totals. Goals, assists and recorded minutes stay visible so visitors can read the rate in its proper context.

decisions.title: Preserve missing observations
decisions.body: An unavailable age or metric stays unavailable. Differing player and season coverage is an explicit property of the archive.

findings: The portfolio offers an interactive five-player comparison from the saved club-league archive.
Recorded totals and per-90 rates can be compared at the same age, including explicit missing-age states.
Screenshots preserve the broader comparison workspace and World Cup data center.
limitations: Source repository is private; the portfolio uses local project captures. A public live deployment was not verified.
Coverage differs by player, season and source. These are recorded club-league summaries, not a universal measure of player quality.
playerpulse.next: Expand and audit comparable coverage before making claims across additional players, competitions or seasons.

intelligence.title: From scattered signals to context.
intelligence.lede: A research workspace that puts company activity, hiring and supporting evidence into the same view.
intelligence.question: How can fragmented company signals become an explainable research workflow?
intelligence.purpose: Help a researcher move from a broad signal summary to the evidence behind it.
intelligence.role: React + FastAPI application · database services · automated workflows
intelligence.evidenceType: Original application interface · fictional API fixtures
intelligence.data: The reviewed project adds Insight Engine, Talent Radar and Scraper Lab. Portfolio screenshots use labelled fictional API fixtures; the Talent Radar walkthrough uses 60 synthetic jobs across four fictional companies.
intelligence.approach: Collect and aggregate company signals, surface trends and hiring capability lanes, and keep source context attached to a researcher’s drill-down.

decisions.title: Organize around research questions
decisions.body: Insight Engine, Talent Radar and Scraper Lab separate company context, hiring patterns and collection inspection into focused modules.

decisions.title: Connect summaries to evidence
decisions.body: Company views and hiring filters let visitors investigate which signals or roles underpin a broader pattern.

decisions.title: Make the walkthrough reproducible
decisions.body: Labelled fictional fixtures demonstrate the interface and filter behavior without claiming those companies, jobs or production records are real.

findings: Three new intelligence modules join scoring services and automated n8n workflows.
The original interface is presented with labelled fictional sample data.
The portfolio walkthrough filters 60 fictional roles by company, market and capability.

metrics.label: Intelligence modules
metrics.context: Insight Engine · Talent Radar · Scraper Lab

limitations: Screenshots and the portfolio walkthrough use fictional fixtures, rather than production company intelligence.
Production data requires the project backend and database. The portfolio does not demonstrate deployed scraping performance or measured research productivity.
intelligence.next: Validate collected signals against source provenance and real researcher workflows before measuring decision quality or production impact.

country.title: Turn curiosity into a place on the map.
country.lede: A geography arcade that connects visual exploration with a reason to keep practising.
country.question: How can map exploration and recall practice work together in one approachable experience?
country.purpose: Let visitors explore, practise and play from the same country model.
country.role: Interactive maps · game rules · responsive browser experience
country.data: The reviewed application covers 195 countries and connects map exploration, country and capital challenges, flag games and private multiplayer rooms.
country.approach: Share the country model across the map and game modes, then use challenge rules, scoring and room flows to turn geographic recognition into interactive practice.

decisions.title: Share the geography model
decisions.body: Country, capital and flag experiences use the same foundation so the arcade remains consistent across exploration and recall challenges.

decisions.title: Give curiosity more than one route
decisions.body: Map exploration and solo challenges make the geography approachable without requiring a multiplayer session.

decisions.title: Keep optional capabilities optional
decisions.body: Voice support and multiplayer depend on browser or service availability. Solo play and map exploration provide independent ways to use the application.

findings: The geography arcade includes 195 countries.
Map exploration, country and capital challenges, flag games and private rooms are brought into a single application.
The public app can be opened from the portfolio for a direct demonstration of the game experience.
limitations: Optional voice input depends on browser support.
Multiplayer requires the public room service. No claim of measured learning improvement or classroom effectiveness is made.
country.next: Evaluate challenge difficulty and accessibility with learners before drawing conclusions about learning outcomes.

agoda.title: A booking analysis you can follow.
agoda.lede: A reproducible analytical workflow with visible validation, useful groupings and interactive exploration.
agoda.question: How do booked rates and lead times vary across a selected set of booking records?
agoda.purpose: Make the path from validated records to booking summaries easy to inspect and reproduce.
agoda.role: Python analysis · input validation · notebook and CLI workflow
agoda.data: The portfolio uses 1,000 deterministic synthetic bookings generated by the updated analysis script with seed 42. All 1,000 rows pass validation; five synthetic cities are represented. The original workbook is absent.
agoda.approach: Validate booking fields, report excluded records, build nonoverlapping lead-time groups, then export six charts and matching CSV summaries from a shared notebook and CLI implementation.

decisions.title: Validate before aggregating
decisions.body: The workflow reports valid and excluded rows so every chart has a visible relationship to the input it summarizes.

decisions.title: Make the groups nonoverlapping
decisions.body: Booking lead-time intervals use explicit boundaries. The same definitions power the chart outputs and the interactive explorer.

decisions.title: Label the synthetic demonstration
decisions.body: A fixed seed makes the walkthrough reproducible while keeping the absence of the original business workbook visible. Booked rates describe the sample; they do not forecast room prices.

findings: The reproducible workflow generates six chart outputs and CSV summaries.
The fixed-seed demonstration contains 1,000 validated bookings and zero excluded rows.
Portfolio controls recalculate counts and mean booked daily rates from the same exported records.
limitations: The original workbook is absent. All portfolio charts and filters use deterministic synthetic bookings.
These results are neither Agoda business findings nor a room-price forecast. No causal conversion effect is established.
agoda.next: Apply the validated workflow to an authorized original workbook before making business recommendations.
